principles: Every false alarm in these transcripts was caught by a control, never by re-reading; a negative is unattributed until a positive control shares its address (learned >=10 times before being written down).
Null/absent key != zero; SurrealDB CONTAINS is an array op; datetime > 'string' matches everything; NONE != NULL; default LIMIT with worst-first sort biases samples.
Local PDT vs container/commit UTC produced false zeros twice; query origin/dev, not a local un-fetched clone.
Intermediate states (stage->commit window, mid-write file, running dispatch) read as terminal — wait past the window.
Count registrations/rows, not a 200 or log lines; measure at the unit the selector selects over (output shape), not name stems.
A gate or detector must be proven to fire and to go red, not merely to exist; a gate that reads a diff cannot certify behaviour.
Retractions must reach state (status: rejected), not prose — a retracted-in-summary gap kept winning compose slots.
Under a standing 'find compounding' instruction with unlimited attempts something will look positive by chance; refuse to keep generating interventions (09-08).
User: 'It always seems like there is another problem of the same class just one stage earlier.' / 'every defect is the same one, one level up'.
User: 'termination is a failure mode, falling off the manifold' — detecting and crossing horizons is the core mechanism.
User: 'Don't put decisions to me… the system needs to know the consequences… causally associate its actions with observable changes on any horizon.'
User: 'cost is not a concern, truth is.'
User: an autonomous system should try alternate routes and verify when the obvious path is wrong or unavailable (what would a human do).
User: docs are invalid the second they are written; names, tables and implementation details are irrelevant — write invariants and failure modes.
User: bring-up should be: basic config, run container, everything works, vessel-ctl for inventory.
User: always sync with the remote; never copy files into the container.
Operator corrections were about abstraction level, not facts; token-level compliance that preserves the defect class is not a fix.
